items.title: How to separate human from non-human visits in webserver access logs?

Most of the sites are low-volume, so the majority of visits is from bots: crawlers from search engine operators, SEO optimizers, vulnerability scanners, etcetera. Such automated visits must be excluded from the analysis as much as possible. 100% accuracy isn't required, but 90% would be nice. Are any tools or resources available for doing this?

With one exception, the same tests on other models at those providers were not accessed, and none of the AWS test keys were used. Your account sent 21 requests to MiniMax models through MiniMax, Novita, StreamLake and AtlasCloud, from June 22 at 03:02 to July 3 at 23:28 UTC.

items.title: How do we get 1 TW a year of orbital compute by 2035?
items.summary: - 50k Starship V4 launches a year, each carrying 200 t (20 MW of compute). That’s 137 a day, one every 2 minutes in two windows of roughly 5–7am and 5–7pm local. As Earth spins, the launch site passes under that target orbit twice a day, at local dawn and local dusk. Globally we’re at about 1 launch a day right now. - The always-sunlit orbit needs launches heading north or south over open water. On US coasts only south works, and packing every usable spot with Starship pads gets us to just 25–30 launches a day. We need 5× that. - So we will go out to sea, 300 km off central California.

items.title: Tool: Kiri
items.summary: Docker Desktop alternative. What we like: Single, Docker-compatible daemon (CLI, Compose, buildx). Performance optimized with a small memory footprint. Includes networks, volumes, k8s. Dev tools like auto-HTTPs endpoints with publicly sharable URLs. Supports macOS, Windows, Linux. What we dislike: Non-native UI, unlike something like Orbstack (which is macOS only). “Machines” are containers with filesystem access, not true VMs.

items.title: Tool: Jiff
items.summary: Datetime library for Rust. What we like: Understands timezones natively and handles daylight sayings. Built-in handling of common date operations like durations, differences, calculations, geo regions. Uses Rust-native formatting and display options, including friendly formats. What we dislike: Shows you how complex dates and times actually are, but that probably means fewer bugs!
